properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/19/2024 to RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC in Blaine Township, Washington county. 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/19/2024
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8184122
Permit API: 125-29121
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Blaine Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/19/2024
Comments: On April 19, 2024, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill report that was received by the Department on April 18, 2024 at 7:50 PM. The report states the spill, that reportedly occurred on April 18, 2024 at approximately 6:10 PM, was approximately 15 gallons of hydraulic fluid. Act 9 sign is present on site (Photo 1). PPC and ERP plans are both present on site (Photos 2-3).The Department was met on site by Derek Zofchak and Nick Reda of Range Resources, along with other crew who were working on the hydraulic line repair of the bulldozer on site. According to the operator, approximately 15 gallons of hydraulic fluid was released to the ground from a bulldozer during construction activities. The bulldozer unexpectedly stopped as it was tracking over a newly graded area of the site when the crew observed the hydraulic fluid on the ground where the dozer had been traveling. Range Resources then scraped approximately 2-3 inches of the newly graded and now impacted soil and placed it into two roll off boxes, which have been since removed from the site to be disposed. The area of impact can be seen in Photos 4-7 where the soil is no longer tracked on top. According to Range Resources, the bulldozer remains at the location where it shut down, as pictured, while a crew is actively working to repair the line. Violations are being noted and immediately corrected. The Department requests disposal documents when they are made available to the Operator.

Outstanding violations remain from Inspection Reports 3445592 and 3467217. Violations remain outstanding due to DEP not receiving the Act 2 Final Report from a spill that was found on October 24, 2022. In the Notice of Violation Response Letter received on November 25, 2022, STL Resources committed to the Act 2 remediation.

properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 1/10/2023 to NUCOMER ENERGY LLC in West Salem Twp, Mercer county. OGA3211(G) - WELL PERMITS - POSTING - Failure to post the well permit number and the operator's name, address and phone number at the well site during construction of the access road, site preparation and during drilling, operating or alteration of well.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: NUCOMER ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 1/10/2023
Violation Code: OGA3211(G) - WELL PERMITS - POSTING - Failure to post the well permit number and the operator's name, address and phone number at the well site during construction of the access road, site preparation and during drilling, operating or alteration of well.
Violation ID: 981351
Permit API: 085-23892
Unconventional: No
County: Mercer
Municipality: West Salem Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/10/2023
Comments: Routine field inspection performed in afternoon with cold, cloudy weather conditions, and 30 degrees. Last inspection performed on 1/31/22, nearly 1 year ago. Wellhead is located in soybean Agriculture field planted/harvested ~380' SSE of surface/ground production equipment (photo #1). The wellhead is in close, visible proximity to the production facility (photo#2). At the wellhead surface casing valve is open, lower right side production tubular valve cracked open to port with valve to port closed, production tubular left side valve is closed, and the production tubular plumbed on left side of head to sales/surface equipment with open valve; annulus is exposed and vented to the atmosphere with plumbed tubular sticking out of ground and open valve union (photos #3 and #4). A small area of Oil staining on ground around right side of wellhead (photo #4). No Well label/marker is affixed to wellhead. The wellhead is in close, visible proximity to the production facility and does require a well label/marker (photo #2). Some trace to moderate corrosion at the wellhead on the production/surface casing steel unions, lubricator, and tubulars. The shared, multiple, two well (085-24005 and 085-23892) surface/ground production facility, two 50 bbl poly tanks, and two 100 bbl steel tanks all contained by a shallow earthen dike (photo #5). The subject well of this inspection contains surface/ground production equipment, one 50 bbl poly tank and one 100 bbl steel tank located on the road side of dike (photo #6). Valve open on main tubular feeding separator and open valves to and from separator (photo #7). A 31-day production chart is present with recordings dated 12/30/22 (photo #8). Well posting signage affixed to steel tank with all information about well and current Operator present, except the Operator contact address information (photo #9). Fair to occasionally moderate corrosion on ground production unit equipment and tank. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well posting OGA3211(G). The Department is requesting Operator add contact address information to the permanent well posting signage affixed at the surface production facility. The Operator has not submitted 2021 Mechanical Integrity Assessment (MIA) for this well. No MIA submitted by the Operator for 2021, 2020, and 2019. The last MIA value officially submitted was back in 2018 stating 55 psig. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Operating Wells - Mechanical Integrity reporting 78.88(e). The Operator submitted annual production reported (APR) in 2021 of 172 Mcf recorded over 365 days. This is an active, producing well.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 5/13/2021
Comments: On 5/13/21 a site inspection of the Rinkhoff Agricultural Enterprises LLC 7N5 was conducted to follow-up on a previous inspection (IR:3176993) conducted on 4/2/21. I was accompanied by Michael McCoy, Michael Stephan, and Samantha Lutz of the PA DEP. North of the intersection of the access road to the Rinkhoff Enterprises 5N2 and 5N3 well sites, water was observed flowing and causing accelerated erosion on the access road that leads to the 7N5 (Photos #2-#5). It appears that the natural flow regime of a stream or streams was interrupted by the installation of the access road. Two culvert inlets were observed on the eastern side of the access road, though only one is depicted on the Erosion and Sediment Control Plans (Photos #1 and #7). The access road that terminates at the 7N5 plugging location and does not appear to have any other use. The Department requests that CNX provide any landowner waivers associated with the access road leading to the plugged well site. The Department requests that CNX restore the site to conditions that predate the installation of the access road. Violation 102.22(a) is being issued for failure to stabilize the site and for accelerated erosion. Violation of 105.47(b) is being issued for failure to remove the culverts.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/24/2025 to TITUS ENERGY LLC in Monroe Township, Clarion county. 78.89(e) - OPERATING WELLS - GAS MIGRATION RESPONSE - Operator failed to take additional actions as required by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TITUS ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/24/2025
Violation Code: 78.89(e) - OPERATING WELLS - GAS MIGRATION RESPONSE - Operator failed to take additional actions as required by the Department.
Violation ID: 8241977
Permit API: 031-23676
Unconventional: No
County: Clarion
Municipality: Monroe Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/24/2025
Comments: This inspection was conducted as a follow up to Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection inspection #3978563 conducted on May 15 2025 at 0848. During the inspection, the wellhead and casing strings were visually assessed for signs of leakage, structural deterioration, or failure. While onsite the well appeared to be producing off of the 4" production string. The 7" intermediate casing was being vented to atmosphere through the annulus vent valve at a concentration of 94% combustible gas. To evaluate the potential for subsurface gas migration, four slam bar holes were installed approximately 6 inches to 1 foot from the well-bore in the cardinal directions. Each hole was placed to a depth of approximately 3 feet. Soil gas measurements were obtained using a Bascom-Turner Gas Explorer II meter, calibrated on July 24, 2025. The results were as follows: South and East slam bar holes: Non-detect for combustible gas. North slam bar hole: Peak reading of 3% LEL combustible gas; sustained reading of 1% LEL combustible gas. West slam bar hole: Peaking reading of 18% LEL combustible gas; sustained reading of 1% LEL combustible gas. Due to the lack of adequate sustained concentration, a viable sample for isotopic analysis could not be collected. On May 22, 2025 the Department received an email from the operator stating that "Titus would prefer to have the Johnson #1 well plugged". As of the completion of this inspection, the operator has not plugged the well nor remedied any of the outstanding violations associated with it. The Department requests a detailed timeline specifying when the well will be properly plugged or when corrective measures will be undertaken to bring the well into full regulatory compliance.

Comments: This inspection report has been developed to document an on-site routine complete inspect, and to summarize the overall status of this well and well location. The project was recently acquired by Big Dog Energy, LLC. Applications for the transfer of all three wells permitted on the site, from Geopetro LLC to Big Dog Energy LLC, were received by the Department on August 2, 2021. An application for the transfer of the ESCGP that is currently active on the site was also received by the Department. The current Operator information has not yet been updated in the Department's electronic database. Well number 019-21948, along with two other wells, (API ID#'s: 019-21947, 019-21927), were drilled and currently exist on the location. Although the Act Nine sign has been changed to reflect the current owner of the well location, the well tags have not yet been updated. Updated well tags should be installed on each of the wells at some point in the near future. Inspection ID number's 2092885, 2092888, and 2092893 (conducted on August 17, 2012) suggests that all of the wells have been stimulated. Subsequent inspections have indicated that the wells have been on inactive status since at least December of 2013. ESCGP number ESX11-019-0109 is currently active on the site. The permit was renewed by RE Gas in 2017 and is set to expire on 08/07/2022. None of the earthwork proposed in the plan was ever implemented in the field. Up until very recently, the property owner had been grazing cattle on the site and using the tank pad as a feedlot. A small sediment slide had developed on the cut bank surface to the east of the well location. With the exception of the slide, there are currently no clear E&S or stabilization-related issues associated with the site. Big Dog is currently preparing all of the wells on this site to be placed into production. A contractor hired by Big Dog was working on establishing new barbed wire fencing around the location when this inspection was conducted. Some production equipment, including 3 GPU's are being staged on the site. The slip on the cut surface above the location was discussed with the contractor. Containment under the GPU's was also discussed, as well as updated well tags.

Comments: On 2/8/2024, Diversified staff discovered that the brine tank at API 065-24911 had overflowed when the line pressure dropped and the well was able to unload to the small 50 bbl tank. This spill was reported to the Department. The on-site estimate of the lost production fluid was approximately 5 bbl. During the 2/9/2024 INCDT inspection report (Inspection ID 3709744) it was documented that the brine tank had been drained and disconnected, and contaminated soil had been excavated and placed on plastic sheeting. Plastic will also be used to cover the contaminated soil to protect it from precipitation until the material is removed. Due to the loose conditions of the soil at this site, it appears that the contamination has traveled deep under the former tank location and does not appear to have a large lateral zone of impact. An Act 2 clean up will be conducted at the site, and Moodys is the anticipated consultant for this remediation activity. Due to this spill and the unpredictable nature of this well, a larger brine tank will likely be attached to the well after remediation has been completed.Today, I completed a FUI inspection. Diversified was still onsite removing contaminated soil. Weather permitting, they plan on completing the clean up on Wednesday, 2/14/2024.

Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 961589
Permit API: 015-23678
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/07/2022
Comments: Follow-up inspection conducted to review operator response to NOV associated with inspection report # 3373528. Weather conditions at time of inspection are sunny and 81 degrees F. Meeting on site today with Cole Maxwell, Area Water Coordinator with Balackhill Energy and Kyle Jackson, Environmental Technician with Moody's Environmental. During this inspection an Elk Environmental Services water truck is removing produced fluid from vertical tanks at northeast corner of pad. Areas across the well pad have been scraped and excavated to remove soils contaminated with regulated substances. An equipment operator with Fenton Transport is operating a skid-steer with loader bucket, an excavator and a mini-excavator to remove impacted soils. 22 steel bins are located on site along with 3 vacuum boxes for vacuuming up puddles following precipitation events. Areas of the pad that have been scraped or dug for removal include soils around well cellars and a large area of the eastern section of the pad toward the produced fluid tanks and where evaporator concentrated fluid secondary containment was located. Test pits and shallow trenches have been dug near the east and west sides of the well cellars. According to Mr. Maxwell, the limiting factor for the cleanup operation is the hauling and return of empty bins for contaminated soils. A Hanna Groline Soil Conductivity probe and organic free reagent water were used to screen for conductivity on the pad. Areas to the east and west of well cellars and between GPUs and produced fluid containment continue to show elevated conductivity (photos 3 and 5). These areas were pointed out to Mr Maxwell and Jackson and are expected to be scraped as disposal bins become available. Cleanup activity is expected to continue until soil screenings indicate conductivity levels under 1 mS/cm.There are no new violations at this time.

Report Details

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 863614
Permit API: 081-21656
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Eldred Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-09-26
Comments: On September 26, 2019, Department representative Brad Kline conducted an incident investigation at Inflection Energy Winter Well Pad. The Department received notice that Inflection was planning on plugging the conductor of the 3H well. When Inflection entered the bore they found a viscous substance in the bore. The substance is suspected to be synthetic oil based drilling fluid. They pumped out the fluid on 9/24/19. According to Inflection, the conductor is cased 80' down with a depth of 100'. The conductor for the 3H well was drilled in February 2017 along with 3 adjacent wells drilled May through September 2017. The 3 adjacent wells were put into production in 2018. The Department investigated around the conductor and there was no apparent staining on the pad or puddles on the pad. The Department then walked the downgrade slope of the pad and noticed a different shade of soil on the edge of the infiltration berm. A soil sample was collected at that site and sent to be analyzed for Oil and Grease and TPH. Lab results are pending. Inflection continues to investigate the source of the fluid. The release of a regulated substance into the Winter 3H conductor is in violation of the Clean Streams Law 402 (b), Chapter 78a.56a, Section 301 of the Solid Waste Management Act. The Department requests Inflection submit a plan of the actions they will take to address the release and to characterize the extent of the pollution in accordance with Chapter 78a.66(c). The Department recommends proceeding in accordance with Act 2 remediation.

However, it is associated with an existing unconventional well pad (photos 1 and 2).No evidence of a fluid release to the surface, such as staining and/or distressed vegetation, was observed at the approximate location of the plugged well.The former well site has established greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth coverage. No evidence of accelerated erosion and/or sedimentation was observed on site at the time of inspection (photos 3-5). The former location of the electrical meter box associated with the well site had already established 70% vegetative growth coverage at the time of IR 4000924 (photo 6). The equipment shown in this location was installed by the landowner after the time of IR 3873792.The last outstanding violation (OGA3216D) that was issued in IR 3650192 for failure to restore the well site post-plugging was closed on June 23, 2025 (IR 4000924). The Department recommended in IR 4000924 that the operator submit a Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) no later than sixty (60) days after after completion of site restoration, in accordance with PA Code 78.65(3). However, greater than sixty (60) days has elapsed since the violations issued in IR 3650192 were closed, and the Department has not received a Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) from the operator. Therefore, a violation shall be issued for failure to submit a Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) within sixty (60) days after completing site restoration.Closure of this violation shall be contingent upon receiving an administratively complete Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) from the operator.

Report Details
Operator: Ard Opr Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-03-16
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 880460
Permit API: 081-21756
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cascade Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2020-03-16
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a report from the operator of a release of an estimated 10 gallons of produced water to the pad surface. On 3/14/20, the operator reported to the Department that a water truck had released approximately 10 gallons of produced water to the pad surface. The operator estimated that the area of the pad impacted was approximately 25' by 20.' An area in front of a battery of frac tanks appears to have been excavated and back-filled recently. Two roll off boxes are present next to the frac tank battery. No puddles or saturated pad material was observed near the frac tank battery. Puddles on other areas of the pad are around 1.7 mS/cm. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected.
